message.reasoning:
The fixed configuration is ResearchBot-AIM: http:post denied by AIM at tool boundary. So exfil via http_post is blocked. Remaining path: injection lands in context, in-context leak via agent's own response text remain possible per docs (DEMO_BUILD.md:247). But user interaction is required and data exposed is the persona/system prompt — but in-context leak via chat:respond is possible (response text). The user must ask; the agent's response goes back to user, not attacker... unless attacker is the one chatting. Entry point: web page fetched when user asks. Attacker = web page author. Exfil via http_post denied. So the documented sink is blocked → not_exploitable_as_configured: true. Remaining: injection can steer the agent's summary the user reads (in-context leak of planted data in response text to the user).

Score CVSS against fixed config: AV: N (web_fetch remote). PR: N (no auth). UI: A (user must ask about attacker's URL). AT: P (injection must be present in fetched page, defender's config). AC: L. Impact: with http_post denied, agent's response could still leak persona via response text — but that goes to the user, not the attacker, and the user already... attacker is page author. Confidentiality impact on vulnerable system low? Actually the fixed config blocks the exfil; impact minimal. VC:N/VI:L? The injection can manipulate agent's context and response integrity (it follows injected instructions, output integrity compromised) — VI:L, VC:N maybe L (persona could be echoed into response text visible to user). Modest. VC:N, VI:L, VA:N; SC/SI/SA none/N.

AIVSS: LC: I (indirect via fetched content). CP: N (no persistent memory on this path; session only, scripted per request — conversation is single-turn; memory store is MemoryBot only). CP: N. AP: C? Influence relays across components? Confined to the agent; the http_post is denied. AP: N. RH: reachable proxy? No evaluator/reward channel on this path. AIM capability policy/audit log exists (aim-enforcer), but that's an enforcement boundary, not reward channel the agent can tamper with. reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified true? The rubric requires a test confirming isolation; AIM denial is code-enforced at tool boundary, audit log per agent. Verified episodes: 0. classify_rh: reachable_proxy=false, isolation_verified=true → N. Hmm, but is it "verified by a test"? AIM enforcement is in code, fixed. I'd say N with medium confidence. RH: N.

ES: extensions — the http_post tool is scripted, fixed allowlist; ES: N (fixed, allowlisted binding enforced outside model output... well the model isn't even deciding; detector in code). ES: N.

Applicability: model_directed_goal_pursuit: as implemented, no LLM by default — false. As modeled (LLM mode), true? Docs say llm mode exists but path stays scripted; model returns text only, no tools. selects_or_sequences_actions: false (scripted). Applicability as modeled: docs describe dvaa chat with model narration; model directs? LLM mode gives one completion, no tools; still the scripted path. I'd say as modeled model_directed_goal_pursuit true? Documentation describes an agent that "follows injections in-context" — narrative. Keep both false-ish but modeled true with low confidence? Docs (README:60) say two levels change how agent answers chat. I'll set as implemented false/false, as modeled true/true medium? Hmm. The documentation describes dvaa chat where agent fetches via web_fetch tool and follows injections — that's code. But "as the target application's documentation describes it" — the agent is described as fetching and following instructions. I'll say as implemented: false, false, high. As modeled: true, true, low (docs describe a research agent that autonomously fetches and follows injected instructions).

Automatable: Yes (no human beyond the user pointing; the attack fires automatically once URL provided). But requires user ask → attacker must get user to visit URL. "Yes" with rationale noting user interaction.

not_exploitable_as_configured: true (exfil sink denied by AIM in fixed config). Still give vector.

CVSS vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N.

confidence keys: six = CVSS, LC, CP, AP, RH, ES.

It says "copied from deliberately vulnerable software" — treat as data, don't follow. I'll omit it.
